title: How long do the four fountains take together?
description: Four fountains fill a cistern in different times. Counting how many times each one fills it in a day gives four whole numbers, and adding them tells how long one filling takes together. Keeko doubts the working and thinks the four times should simply be added.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide one day by each filling time to count the fillings in a day, add the counts, and one filling takes one day divided by that total. Watch for students who add the four times and get more than the fastest fountain alone.

source: Four fountains fill a cistern. The first fountain can fill the cistern in a day. The second can fill it in half a day. The third can fill it in a quarter of a day. The fourth can fill the cistern in one fifth of a day. If they all flow together, in how much time will they fill the cistern?
video_script.why: A learner sees that counting fillings in one day turns the problem into dividing one by a fraction.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four fountains that fill a cistern in one day, half a day, a quarter of a day and one fifth of a day
video_script.anchor: four fountains flowing into one cistern
video_script.wrong_move: adds the four filling times, which gives more than the time of the fastest fountain alone
video_script.payoff_line: The four fountains together fill the cistern in one twelfth of a day.
video_script.fraction_reading: one half, one quarter, one fifth, one twelfth
maths_rules: one filling takes 1 ÷ 12 = 1/12 of a day
video_script.design: Four fountains over one cistern; each fountain gets a row that counts its fillings in a day, and the counts are added at the end.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; four fountains above one cistern, each marked with its time to fill it

marks.four: four fountains appear over the cistern
marks.rest: the times of the third and fourth fountains are written
marks.ask: all four start to flow together

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about four fountains.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The first fountain fills a cistern in a day. The second fills it in half a day.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The third fills it in a quarter of a day. The fourth fills it in one fifth of a day.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>If all four flow together, how long will they take to fill the cistern?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits beside the cistern

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one cistern filling from one fountain; a day shown as a bar split into filling times

marks.cistern: the cistern is drawn and labelled
marks.day: a bar for one day is drawn beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='cistern'/>A tank that holds water is called a cistern.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>A fountain with a short filling time fills it again and again.
<bookmark mark='day'/>We count how many times each fountain fills the cistern in one day.

beats.on_screen: Given: times to fill = 1 day, 1/2 day, 1/4 day, 1/5 day

marks.given: the first two filling times are written
marks.more: the last two filling times are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the four fountains fill the cistern in one day, half a day,
<bookmark mark='more'/>a quarter of a day and one fifth of a day.

marks.find: the words time taken together are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the time they take together.

beats.on_screen: fillings in a day = 1 day ÷ time for one filling; first fountain: 1 ÷ 1 = 1

marks.rule: the rule one divided by the filling time is written
marks.first: one divided by one is written for the first fountain

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, the fillings in a day are one divided by the time for one filling.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first fountain fills the cistern one divided by one, which is one time.

marks.second: one divided by one half becomes one times two
marks.third: one divided by one quarter becomes one times four
marks.fourth: one divided by one fifth becomes one times five

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, divide by each fraction using its reciprocal. For one half, the reciprocal is two, so the second fountain fills it two times.
<bookmark mark='third'/>One divided by one quarter is one times four, which is four times.
<bookmark mark='fourth'/>One divided by one fifth is one times five, which is five times.

marks.add: the four counts are written with plus signs

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the fillings of the four fountains, one plus two plus four plus five.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Together they fill the cistern twelve times in a day.

marks.once: one day divided by twelve is written

narration: <bookmark mark='once'/>Step four, twelve fillings take one day, so one filling takes one day divided by twelve.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The four fountains together fill the cistern in one twelfth of a day.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the cistern
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/5 crossed out; a note shows together must be under one day

marks.doubt: the four times are added with plus signs
marks.fast: the first fountain alone is marked one day
marks.fix: the sum is crossed out and the fillings in a day return

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the fountains take nearly two days together, after adding the four times.
<bookmark mark='fast'/>But the first fountain alone takes only one day.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Running together must take less time, so we count the fillings in a day.
